Data: We will use the same simulation setup that we used in class, but tweak the numbers a little.


```{r, message = FALSE}
# Load necessary libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble) 

# --- 1. Set Simulation Parameters ---

set.seed(123) 

n_per_cell <- 75 
residual_sd <- 2.5

mean_A_Control <- 10
mean_A_TX <- 11

mean_B_Control <- 9
mean_B_TX <- 11

mean_C_Control <- 12
mean_C_TX <- 12

# --- 3. Generate the Data ---

# Create the data for each of the 6 cells
data_A_Control <- rnorm(n_per_cell, mean = mean_A_Control, sd = residual_sd)
data_A_TX <- rnorm(n_per_cell, mean = mean_A_TX, sd = residual_sd)
data_B_Control <- rnorm(n_per_cell, mean = mean_B_Control, sd = residual_sd)
data_B_TX <- rnorm(n_per_cell, mean = mean_B_TX, sd = residual_sd)
data_C_Control <- rnorm(n_per_cell, mean = mean_C_Control, sd = residual_sd)
data_C_TX <- rnorm(n_per_cell, mean = mean_C_TX, sd = residual_sd)

# Combine into a single "long" data frame
simulated_data <- data.frame(
  dv = c(data_A_Control, data_A_TX, data_B_Control, data_B_TX, data_C_Control, data_C_TX),
  Dose = factor(rep(c("A", "A", "B", "B", "C", "C"), each = n_per_cell)),
  Condition = factor(rep(c("Control", "TX", "Control", "TX", "Control", "TX"), each = n_per_cell))
)

```



1. Run two models, a main effects only model and an interaction model, both with Dose and Condition as IVs. 

a. DoseB is significant in one but not the other, why? 

b. For each model, how would you interpret the intercept? Do they test the same hypothesis?

c. Test to see whether you need to include an interaction. What is the null hypothesis of this test? 

d. In summarizing your findings of the best fit model, what effect size estimate(s) would you want to report?

e. Graph a figure of your results. 


2. Run an interaction model with the RSE set to 4. 

a. How does this model change the estimates and SEs? Will they always change in that way if your RSE is larger? How would they change if your RSE was smaller? What can you do to YOUR data to get a smaller RSE? 

b. Should you include an interaction term or go with a main effects model? How do you know? 

c. Assuming you you decide the no interaction model is the best fit, graph your results.

d. Using the interaction model with RSE = 4, what are the estimated cell means and associated standard error? Why can the standard error of the mean be found in the summary output of the regression?  

e. Estimate the simple main effects for both condition and for dose.
